content.intro: Learn using django command-line tools through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Using Django Command-Line Tools matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines using django command-line tools as part of development environment and project setup. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Using Django Command-Line Tools
content_blocks.code:
python manage.py help
python manage.py check
python manage.py check --deploy
content_blocks.expected_output: The commands show available management commands and run general/deployment-oriented checks.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Run from the project root and correct virtual environment; `check --deploy` needs production-like settings and is not a complete security audit.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
